intro.title: The Common Grounds Media Matrix
intro.text: A smooth, slide-based presentation comparing the two countries. It charts shared seafaring history, culinary crossovers and language links, and also covers family, faith, dress, crafts, architecture, music, celebrations and people.

ui.hint: Swipe, scroll or use the arrow keys

slides.title: Sons and Daughters of the Sea
slides.text: Both countries were shaped by the sea. Tunisia's Phoenician settlers founded Carthage around 814 BC and sailed a trading empire across the Mediterranean, while Dilmun made Bahrain a hub of trade between Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley 5,000 years ago. Tunisians fished with the charfia traps of the Kerkennah Islands and gathered sponges off Djerba and Zarzis. Bahrainis dove for pearls for 7,000 years and built wooden ships without a single iron nail.
